A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe the same FSD work, and their main text, equations, tables, and figures are readable. However, v1 ends after the references without the appendices A–J that it cites; v3 includes them. This limits direct comparison of earlier supplementary details.

before.justification: v1 reports original FSD benchmark results, component ablations, SimplerEnv experiments, and eight real-world manipulation tasks.

after.justification: v3 retains original FSD experiments and additionally reports execution times, further baseline comparisons, and qualitative whiteboard-wiping and drawer-opening experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the architecture, SrCoT reasoning, self-consistency mechanism, two-stage training, eight-point traces, and action-execution pipeline. The added coordinate-format and appendix implementation descriptions elaborate existing components without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Section 6.2 adds qualitative evaluation on whiteboard wiping and drawer opening, extending coverage to continuous-contact and articulated-object tasks. The original benchmarks and eight-task real-world evaluation remain. Appendix B details the previously summarized training mixture rather than establishing new training coverage.

E2.justification: Table 4 removes RT-1-X, RoboVLM, and SpatialVLA comparisons and adds π0, π0-fast, OpenVLA-OFT, MOKA, and RoboPoint. Table 3 adds RoboBrain to both VABench tasks and GPT-4o to VisualTrace. Figure 7 also adds MOKA to the real-world comparison, substantially revising the comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 5 changes the reported judge-score range from 0–10 to 1–10. Table 4 removes separate grasp-rate reporting while retaining 24 episodes per task, and Table 5 introduces execution-time evaluation on two retained tasks. Figure 4 corrects its 940k QA label to 300k, matching the existing body text; this does not establish actual dataset resizing.

E4.justification: The SrCoT and alignment ablations remain. v3 adds limited qualitative examinations of contact-rich and articulated manipulation, an execution-latency comparison, and the RoboBrain trajectory case studies now available in Appendix I. These extend supplementary analysis without introducing a broad sensitivity or robustness study.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports training seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Numerical comparisons and success-rate plots remain point estimates without uncertainty bars.

E6.justification: Table 4 changes FSD’s average from 54.1% to 40.6%, correctly averaging unchanged task scores of 41.6%, 50.0%, 33.3%, and 37.5%. Table 3 revises judge scores, including FSD’s 5.49 to 6.21, while retaining its RMSE and MAE; the revised scoring specification prevents interpreting this as a same-setting gain. Baseline results, latency measurements, and qualitative findings are added, while grasp-rate entries disappear. Tables 1–2 remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The newly supplied Appendix C explicitly formulates intermediate-depth optimization by minimizing consecutive 3D path distances with endpoint depths fixed. This adds a mathematical specification beyond v1’s high-level optimization description. The visual-aid definitions and MAE/RMSE equations remain, and neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The methodological contributions remain, but the flagship manipulation claim is materially narrowed. The abstract and introduction change SimplerEnv success from 54.1% to 40.6%, and the introduction attributes the 30% real-world advantage specifically to comparison with RoboPoint rather than mainstream VLAs. Section 6.2 also withdraws the blanket claim of outperforming fine-tuned VLAs.

C2.justification: Beyond v1’s brief limitations concerning 2D representations and data quality, Appendix J discusses explicit-instruction requirements, long-horizon decomposition, and execution bottlenecks in complex or dynamic environments. Section 6.2 qualifies controller readiness for the challenging tasks and adds explanations of MOKA failures and latency. Appendix I develops the object-centric versus agent-centric interpretation of generalization.

D1.justification: v3 supplies extensive previously unavailable documentation: data filtering and generation prompts, training-mixture counts, batch size 128, learning rate 2×10^-5, training epochs, eight A100 GPUs, training times, execution optimization, and baseline implementation details. It also provides code and dataset access information and states that datasets and checkpoints are publicly available.

R1.justification: The three related-work themes and reasoning-based positioning largely remain. Selected references are added for MOKA, FAST, OpenVLA-OFT, InternVLA-M1, and technical resources, while RoboVLM and SpatialVLA references disappear. Appendix I adds a focused positioning comparison with RoboBrain.

P1.justification: Although the main section sequence remains, v3 substantially expands the exposition through structured appendices containing explanations, worked examples, and prompts. It also rewrites the decision-evaluation discussion, expands the SrCoT explanation, and adds acknowledgements, ethics, and reproducibility statements.

P2.justification: v3 changes typography and page layout, redistributes retained figures and tables, expands Table 3, redesigns Table 4 by method category, and updates Figure 7 with MOKA. It adds latency and training-data tables plus rollout, case-study, and appendix figures. Some benchmark examples are redisplayed rather than representing new experiments.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially reduces v1’s reproducibility gap by supplying the missing technical appendices, configurations, and prompts. It also corrects FSD’s inflated SimplerEnv average and narrows the associated superiority claim, while strengthening comparative evidence. These are substantial gains despite a new Table 4 inconsistency: π0-fast is assigned a 48.3% average although its listed task scores average 32.1%, leaving part of the ranking unreliable.
